answer: In an aerial agent economy operating between a coastal inlet and a mountain summit, line-of-sight optical verification curbs Sybil attacks. Ground stations emit narrow laser pulses that drones must retroreflect as they wander across flight paths. An attacker must deploy separate optical transceivers and pointing gimbals per identity, imposing steep hardware costs. However, heavy fog or atmospheric scattering can attenuate beams, causing false verification failures.
